children: Inflation-adjusted hourly earnings have turned negative on a year-over-year basis, adding to pressure on workers as wage growth slows while inflation remains elevated.

Real average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls fell about 0.3% year over year in August, according to the chart from EY-Parthenon, based on Bureau of Labor Statistics data.

The August decline followed a 0.2% year-over-year decline in July, according to the BLS. Real average hourly earnings had increased 0.1% over the 12 months through June before turning negative in July.

Gregory Daco, chief economist at EY-Parthenon, said inflation-adjusted wage growth had contracted for five consecutive months on the measure he cited, describing the development as an income squeeze not seen since 2012, excluding the post-pandemic period when public assistance helped offset the impact.
The chart showed real wage growth had weakened significantly from the positive readings seen through much of 2024 and 2025, eventually slipping below zero in the latest months.
The deterioration meant wage gains were no longer fully keeping pace with inflation, putting pressure on workers' inflation-adjusted earnings and purchasing power.

title: Real wages fall as income squeeze deepens
